#+title: drift-sweep was red on 32 refdata generated files, and regenerating fixed it
#+description: compass check --only drift-sweep failed with 32 files that a render would change, all in ores.refdata generated output. Every diff was clang-format wrapping and include ordering, with no semantic difference, so the gate was reporting formatting drift and not a model disagreement. Regenerating the component with compass codegen regenerate --component refdata --address ores restored all 32 to the content HEAD carries: the working tree had them reformatted away from what the generator produces. The sweep is green afterwards and a second regeneration leaves the 32 clean, so the fix is stable rather than incidental. git status went from 232 to 200 modified paths. Worth knowing because the failure looks like a code change and is only a formatting one, and because the same shape could hide a real drift behind 31 cosmetic ones.

* The cost, learned the same way

=compass codegen regenerate= rewrites every file the component owns, whether or
not the content changes. mtimes move for all of them, so a regeneration that
changes nothing still invalidates the build cache: the next build recompiles
the whole component. Measured here — the =ores.ore.core.tests= build that
started at 00:41 restarted at 730 objects and 40% because the =refdata=
regeneration above had touched the component's sources.

So "regenerate and see if anything changed" is not a read-only drift probe. The
read-only version is to hash the generated tree, regenerate, and hash again.
Use the regeneration itself only when the drift is real.
